selection.note: test split is evaluated for reporting only and never selects the checkpoint

feature_cache.note: opt-in bounded host-RAM retention of extracted records across epochs (train.online_feature_cache_gb; 0 = disabled). A cache hit replaces the target forward for that row; hits/misses are per lookup, evictions are LRU byte-cap evictions, and the cache is runtime-only.

feature_source.target_forwards_note: target_forwards counts model forward calls; target_samples counts extracted rows. They differ when train.online_batch_size > 1 (one forward per capture group).
feature_source.extraction_wall_seconds_note: wall_seconds is the full extraction boundary for one row: render/decode + processor (prepare_seconds) plus the teacher-forced target forward and record finalisation (forward_seconds), with the target device synchronized around each timed stage. Per-sample reads (extract) and batched reads (fetch_batch) charge the same boundary, so their extraction_wall_seconds_total values are comparable. Counters are per phase (train / overfit sanity / calibration); the startup visual-path check runs a fixed 3 capture forwards outside these counters, and a resumed run answers fast-forwarded items with cheap placeholders that consume no target work (counted as fast_forward_items, never as wall_seconds)
feature_source.target_device_peak_note: target_device_peak_gb is the CUDA peak on the target's device during that phase (reset per phase). When target.device == train.device the phase peak includes the trainer's own allocations; on split devices it isolates the target, which target_resident_bytes (weights only) cannot show.
